generation_contract.description: K-21: machine-checkable dynamic-content constraints (docs/03 §12). When present, every activity content_ref/concept_ref must be covered by allowed_vocab/allowed_grammar, and referenced ids must exist in the pack.

capabilities.description: K-67/ADR-0021: feature names this unit declares itself able to serve, from a closed list (not script names or file layout). A capability is a claim the app MAY surface for this unit, not an instruction to run: naming one causes nothing in the engine to execute. `script-introduction` claims the unit's items are the writing-system set a new learner is introduced to first. A claim without content is meaningless, so a unit declaring capabilities must reference at least one content item (`unit_capability_items_missing`). A pack that omits this field keeps existing behavior.

requires_unit.description: K-70/ADR-0022: unit-level phase gate. Every entry must hold before this unit's content items may be selected as NEW material: every content item scheduled by the named unit must have derived mastery at least `state` (in any dimension). Gates combine with AND; an entry naming a unit that is not declared by this pack, naming itself, or closing a gate cycle makes the unit permanently unreachable, so those are validation errors. This is selection order as pack data — the engine matches no script or subject names — and reviews of already-introduced items are never affected. Absence of the field keeps existing behavior.

task_sequence.description: ADR-0037: this unit claims a task sequence that exercises its goal end to end: meaningful input, a scaffolded response, an independent response, the same language in a changed context, and delayed reuse. Each role names exactly one activity id declared by this pack. `input`, `scaffolded` and `independent` name activities of this unit; `transfer` and `reuse` may name activities of a later unit in the same goal. The claim is checkable, not executable: tools/audit_content_templates.py verifies that every named activity has an engine runner, that the scaffolded stage carries support while the independent stage carries none, that the transfer stage really changes context (it names a scenario, or it lives in a different unit that reuses this unit's content), and that the reuse stage's unit is phase-gated on this unit (`task-sequence-*`). Nothing in the engine reads this field; naming a sequence causes nothing to execute. A pack that omits it keeps existing behavior.
